sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Hampden Township, PA?
sections.html:
Selling in Hampden Township means selling into one of the higher-priced, owner-heavy parts of the Harrisburg area. The Census Bureau lists 35,401 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 8.1 percent from the April 2020 base, which makes the township the largest municipality in Cumberland County.

The same Census table puts the owner-occupied rate at 76.9 percent, the median owner-occupied home value at $354,900 and median gross rent at $1,466 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income over that period was $105,434, and 55.3 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Those numbers describe a township where most sellers own a family home with decades of equity, and where buyers expect a house in good order.

If your Hampden house needs work, has tenants, or came to you through an estate, the usual listing path can be slow. That is why many owners compare a traditional sale with a direct as-is purchase before they spend money on repairs.

sections.h2: Where is Hampden Township and what is around it?
sections.html:
Hampden Township sits in the northeastern part of Cumberland County, with the Conodoguinet Creek running east toward the Susquehanna River. It covers about 17.3 square miles of land, with Blue Mountain along the northern edge and the creek bending through the middle.

  • Villages inside the township: Brennemans Mill, Good Hope, Mount Zion and Sporting Hill.
  • Neighbors: East Pennsboro Township, Camp Hill, Lower Allen Township, Shiremanstown, Mechanicsburg and Silver Spring Township, with Rye Township in Perry County to the north.
  • Roads: Interstate 81 crosses the north end with an exit at Mount Zion on Route 944, and Route 581 runs across the township with exits at Creekview Road, the Carlisle Pike (U.S. 11) and Route 641.

The area was settled in 1731 and incorporated on January 23, 1845. The Battle of Sporting Hill took place here in 1863, and the township became a first-class township on January 1, 1960. Growth since then has been steady: the Census count rose from 24,135 in 2000 to 32,761 in 2020.

sections.h2: Which school district serves Hampden Township homes?
sections.html:
The Cumberland Valley School District serves Hampden Township. Its school list includes Eagle View Middle School, Mountain View Middle School and Cumberland Valley High School, plus a group of elementary schools. School district boundaries matter for a sale because the district also sends its own real estate tax bill, covered below.

Hampden also keeps more than 100 acres of parks, including Hampden Pool and Park, Creekview Recreation Area, Salem Community Park and Conodoguinet Youth Park, and it runs Armitage Golf Club on Orrs Bridge Road. Buyers often ask about these, so mention the one closest to your street when you describe the house.

sections.h2: What property taxes and bills come with a Hampden Township house?
sections.html:
Three real estate bills reach a Hampden owner each year: a county bill that also carries the library and township charges, a school district bill, and a separate per capita tax for adults. The township tax collector's FAQ explains the schedule, and the county assesses every property at 100 percent of its 2010 value.

Hampden Township real estate bill calendar, from the township Tax Collector FAQ
BillIssued2 percent discountFace amount10 percent penalty starts
County, library and townshipMarch 1March 1 to April 30May 1 to June 30July 1
Cumberland Valley School DistrictJuly 1July 1 to August 31September 1 to October 31November 1

The same FAQ lists the combined county, library and township millage at 3.031 mills for 2025 (county 2.625, library 0.250, township 0.156) and the school district rate at 11.937 mills for 2024 to 2025. Apply those mills to the assessed value, not to the sale price.

  • County bills cover January 1 through December 31, and school bills cover July 1 through June 30.
  • The per capita tax is $10 at face for each resident 18 or older. It is not prorated, so someone who moves out of the township after March 1 still owes the full year.
  • Landlords must tell the tax collector about tenants over 18 under Chapter 24 of the township code.
  • The state Homestead credit on the school bill was $85.49 for 2024 for residents on file with the county assessor.

Ask the tax collector for a statement of what is owed on your parcel before you sign anything. Questions about assessed value go to the Cumberland County Assessment Office at (717) 240-6350.

sections.h2: What township charges follow a Hampden house at sale?
sections.html:
Trash and stormwater are billed by the township and stay with the property, so settle them before the closing date. The township trash page lists each household's weekly pickup at $117.99 per quarter, and it includes one bulk item a week if you schedule it with the hauler.

The Sewer Authority's stormwater fee was set by a 2015 resolution at $13.25 per equivalent residential unit each quarter, and every single-family home counts as one unit of 3,534 square feet of impervious surface. Ask the township office about the sewer bill and any final reading when you set a closing date.

Leaf collection, yard waste and a bulk pickup schedule are on the township website. A clean, cleared yard helps a buyer walking the property, whether the buyer is a family or an investor.

sections.h2: Do permits and repairs matter before selling in Hampden Township?
sections.html:
Yes, because the township Community Development Department expects permits for most work over $500, and a buyer or lender may ask whether past projects were closed out. The department is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and answers at (717) 761-0119.

  • Building permits cover residential construction above $500 in total cost. Roof re-shingling that is not structural, window replacement, siding, gutters and like-for-like kitchen or bath replacement are listed exceptions.
  • Most standard residential permits are processed within 15 business days.
  • Zoning permits are needed for sheds, fences, accessory buildings and added impervious coverage.
  • A certificate of occupancy proves a building passed final inspection under the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code. The township says the owner, not the contractor, is responsible for making sure it was issued.

If you finished a deck, pool or addition without the last inspection, the stalled paperwork can hold up a conventional sale. A buyer paying cash for the house as it stands may be willing to take that on, but ask the department what it would need.

sections.h2: How does recording and transfer tax work in Cumberland County?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Cumberland County Recorder of Deeds, which keeps records back to 1750 and is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with appointments requested for in-person visits. Call 717-240-6370 to schedule one.

Pennsylvania charges a 1 percent state realty transfer tax, and the Department of Revenue notes that counties collect an additional local share for school districts and municipalities. Transfers by will or intestate succession are exempt from the tax. For Cumberland County, the Department of Revenue's valuation factor is 1.56 for documents accepted from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

Ask your title company for the exact local percentage on your deed and for the split between buyer and seller, since the county pages above do not set it for you.

sections.h2: What are my options for selling a Hampden Township house?
sections.html:
There are three common routes, and the right one depends on the house and your timeline.

  • List with an agent: usually the highest price for a house in good shape, with showings, an appraisal and a lender's timeline to manage.
  • Sell by owner: saves a listing fee but puts marketing, disclosure forms and negotiation on you.
  • Take a cash offer: the buyer purchases as-is, so no showings or repair requests, and you pick the closing date.

For a Hampden house with deferred repairs, an estate to settle or tenants in place, compare the net amount from each route, not just the headline price.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hampden Township house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, a sale can move ahead with an open balance. Ask the township tax collector at (717) 737-4822 for the amount owed on your parcel, hand it to your title company, and they will include it on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Who do I call if I think my Hampden assessment is wrong?
faqs.a: Call the Cumberland County Assessment Office at (717) 240-6350. The township tax collector only bills the assessed value the county provides, so corrections and appeals start with the county.

faqs.q: Do I owe the per capita tax if I sell and move away mid-year?
faqs.a: Yes, if you lived in the township on March 1 when the bills were mailed. The tax collector's FAQ says the bill is not prorated, so you owe the full amount to Hampden Township for that year, not to your new municipality.

faqs.q: Does a Hampden house need a certificate of occupancy to sell?
faqs.a: The township describes the certificate as proof that work under a building permit passed final inspection. If a past project needed a permit, call Community Development at (717) 761-0119 and confirm the final inspection was done before you list.

faqs.q: What does the Hampden stormwater fee cost?
faqs.a: The Sewer Authority set it at $13.25 per equivalent residential unit per quarter in 2015, with single-family homes counted as one unit. Confirm the present amount with the township before closing, since the authority can revise it.
